text: Diego wants this scoped pi-mcp-adapter fork published to npm so The Last Harness can install it via exact npm pins instead of checking out the repository during installer runs; the motivation is faster TLH installation.

Diego decided this fork should follow a non-rebase upstream intake model adapted from pi-subagents: review/adopt upstream by release/tag or coherent feature cluster, integrate via explicit merge or squash-import PRs, and record each intake in .upstream-ledger.jsonl with the git DAG plus ledger treated as authoritative. He explicitly rejected blind per-commit sync/replay and any baseline that would imply post-v2.10.0 upstream adoption without a real intake record. The initial ledger baseline is informational only and marks v2.10.0 as the historical fork base for future intake work.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Diego requires upstream intake reviews for the TLH pi-mcp-adapter fork to treat context/token growth as a first-class compatibility constraint. Features that add persistent tool descriptions, registered tools or commands, server-provided instructions, schemas, status text, or bundled skills must be evaluated for context impact rather than adopted automatically; fixes remain desired, while context-expanding features require an explicit decision.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: For the planned post-v2.11 upstream intake, Diego approved taking the v2.12 bug/security/lifecycle fixes and low-context opt-in capabilities, while excluding automatic per-server instruction snippets and disabled-server name lists from the persistent mcp tool description. The direct-tool hot-loading policy remains deferred until it can be evaluated together with later freezeDirectTools and search-activated direct-tool behavior.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: For the planned upstream intake, Diego approved the v2.13 changes except automatic loading of ~/.agents/mcp.json and ~/.agents/mcp/mcp.json. Those paths may be detected for setup, but activation must require explicit opt-in so they do not unexpectedly add servers/tools or alter the fork’s documented config precedence. includeTools allowlists, JSONC, secure OAuth storage, tracing, status snapshots, and the other v2.13 fixes are approved; direct-tool activation remains deferred.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: For the planned upstream intake, Diego approved the v2.14-v2.17 fixes and opt-in capabilities, including command-backed secrets, rmcp-mux transport, per-server prefixes, OAuth parameters, footer controls, and the large-direct-tool warning. Registration/activation of direct tools in child startup remains deferred for the later combined direct-tool context policy.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: For the planned upstream intake, Diego approved the v2.18-v2.20.1 fixes and features with TLH token-budget defaults: freezeDirectTools defaults true; mcpScript implementation is available but scriptMode defaults false; its skill is manual-only; the persistent mcp description must not mention mcpScript when scripting is disabled; child agents remain proxy-only unless tools are explicitly selected. Ranked paginated search and compact TypeScript schema rendering are approved as token-saving behavior.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: For the planned upstream intake, Diego approved all v2.21-v2.24 changes with secure/context-bounded defaults: Agent Plugin MCP loading stays explicit-path only with no auto-discovery; OAuth issuer validation remains enabled unless explicitly overridden; searchKeywords remain model-invisible; app-only tools remain hidden; binary resources use bounded private-file references; and the prior token/config exclusions continue.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: For the planned upstream intake, Diego approved all v2.25-v2.27 changes with context safeguards: package-manifest MCP servers are forced proxy-only unless user config explicitly overrides them; runtime registrations remain proxy-only; the persistent mcp description is fixed/bounded and omits dynamic direct-tool lists, enabled/disabled server summaries, and instruction snippets, mentioning mcpScript only when enabled; requestHeadersCommand stays explicit and is documented as seeing complete outbound requests.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: For the planned upstream intake, Diego approved all released v2.28-v2.32.1 changes with safeguards: namespace proxy tools are available only through an explicit setting and default off; shared-config setup writes require explicit user action and preview, defaulting to project .mcp.json; adapter-only settings remain in Pi-owned overrides; all prior token-budget and config-discovery decisions remain in force.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Diego decided not to intake any post-v2.32.1 upstream/main commits yet. The planned upstream intake stops at the released v2.32.1 boundary; unreleased fixes and features will be investigated again after they appear in an upstream release.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Diego requires pi-mcp-adapter upstream intake boundaries to use released upstream tags only. Commits present only on upstream/main are considered unsafe for intake and must wait for a release before review or adoption.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Diego approved extending the reviewed upstream intake boundary from v2.11.0 through released tag v2.36.0 only. Adopt the reviewed fixes and optional features while excluding model-facing URL installation and Jev/TypeSafe integration, preserving TLH context/config safeguards and fork deltas; no commits after v2.36.0 may be included.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Observed during the 2026-10-03 v5 intake: the read-only reviewer child bash inherited MCP_DIRECT_TOOLS=__none__, while architect bash reported it unset. This discrepancy hid the keep-alive input gate in the child reproduction until env -u MCP_DIRECT_TOOLS was used. Do not infer child test environments from the parent shell; run relevant validations with the override explicitly unset and ensure input-path regressions exercise their intended branch.
author: The Last Harness <hi@thelastharness.com>

text: For the v5.0.0 intake on 2026-10-04, Diego approved affected-server-only panel Save refresh under freezeDirectTools rather than amending the ticket to preserve HEAD's all-server Save refresh. This is an intentional compatibility departure from the shipped fork, not a regression introduced by this intake; retain all-server reconciliation when freezeDirectTools is false.
author: The Last Harness <hi@thelastharness.com>

text: For the v5.0.0 intake, Diego approved strict freeze for already-applied direct-tool surfaces across input, passive metadata and reconnect paths, with one first-discovery exception per search-mode server per session to retain cold search behavior. The exception touches only a never-applied server; a valid cached empty catalog counts as applied, and later emptying or reconnecting does not renew eligibility. All other applied servers, including other search-mode servers, remain pinned. This supplements the affected-server-only persisted panel Save decision; the alternative of leaving cold search proxy-only until reload/Save was not chosen.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Human clarification approved 2026-10-05 during released-v5 intake failure triage: retain scriptMode off and manual skill default, but honor explicitly configured scriptSkill:model by adding the upstream skill path to the opted-in mcpScript description. This is an explicit narrow clarification of wxcxnb manual-only wording, not permission for automatic skill invocation/injection or scripting enablement. Adopt upstream v5 opt-in mcpScript result guidance. Restore native sign-in offer at UI session startup with current filtered config, cancellable ownership/first-use fencing; native settings/auth files stay read-only. Adapter-owned auth and piSignInImportsAsked bookkeeping may be written only following a live current-session user response; builtin-settings disabling/bookkeeping remains excluded. Existing pre-session eager/keep-alive connections remain outside this import-before-connect guarantee; no authorization to defer/change them or claim they are covered. Actual config/cache/keyring/services are untouched during implementation/validation; tests use isolated owned fixtures. All earlier freeze/trust/worker isolation/defaults remain unchanged.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>
